title: The Loud Sound
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 1, week 1 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds ay, ou, ie
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'ou' (as in out, loud, sound). Children already know 'ow' for this sound from 'cow' — this shows them the other common spelling. Every other word uses only Phase 2 to 4 sounds, so it stays fully decodable.

pages.text: It was dark. Pip was in bed.
pages.illustration: Pip curled up in the ivy nest at night, one wing over his head, tiny and cosy. Deep blues, one small warm spot of colour on him.

pages.text: Out in the night, a loud sound!
pages.illustration: The same nest from outside, tiny in a huge dark garden, with the night suddenly loud — show it as every leaf and branch drawn sharp and startled. No visible source yet.
Extreme close-up of Pip's face, eyes enormous, feathers on end, gripping the nest edge. The whole page is his fright.
Pip climbing cautiously out over the rim of the nest into the dark, one foot testing the branch. Brave and very small.

pages.text: Up in the oak sat Olive the owl.
pages.illustration: Reveal page: Olive the owl on a branch above, lit by the moon, entirely unbothered, mid-hoot. Draw her big and round and slightly ridiculous.

pages.text: Olive let out a loud hoot.
pages.illustration: Olive's hoot from Pip's viewpoint — Olive close and enormous, beak wide, Pip a tiny silhouette in the corner of the frame.

pages.text: The loud sound was just Olive!
pages.illustration: Pip and Olive face to face on the branch, Pip's relief written all over him, Olive faintly apologetic. Warm despite the night palette.
Pip flying back to the nest with his shoulders down, calm now. The garden drawn friendly again — soft edges instead of sharp ones.
Pip tucked back in, eyes shut, one wing over his head exactly as on page one. Same composition as page one so children spot the echo.
Closing page: wide still garden at night, the oak, the nest, the moon, Olive a small shape on her branch keeping watch. Deeply peaceful.
